transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-04-03 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Sofia A (Redwood AE), Marcus C (Redwood SE), Priya K (Redwood CSM), Emma L (Cerulean Head ML), Ravi P (CTO), Jenna T (Lead SRE)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy QBR. Quick check — audio ok?
[00:08] Emma: Yep, all good.
[00:12] Sofia: Great. I'll kick off with a quick ops summary, Priya will go through health metrics, Marcus will cover performance deep-dive notes, and then we'll do next steps.
[00:23] Priya: Quick context — Cerulean has been on Redwood Hosted since Jan, moved a portion of high-throughput jobs to our cache layer in Feb. Monthly token usage is ~22M tokens now, up from 16M last quarter, so about 38% growth.
[00:37] Ravi: Yeah growth driven by more real-time analytics features. Cost is a little higher than we expected — the bill for March was $12.4k vs $8.1k in Jan.
[00:49] Sofia: Right, cost went up mainly because of model mix — more use of larger LLMs for summarization and longer context windows. We'll send the model-by-model breakdown after this call.
[01:03] Marcus: On reliability — we saw two incidents in March: one transient 503 in us-west-2 on 3/11 that lasted ~14 minutes, and a KV-cache miss storm that increased tail latency for a subset of requests. Both were within our SLO for availability but did affect some batches. Noted that the cache miss was due to a backend policy mismatch, so it's fixable.
[01:28] Jenna: That 503 spike coincided with a deploy on your side? We saw retries stack up.
[01:34] Marcus: There was a coordinated kernel rollout in our serving runtime that morning — the rollout hit a small fleet with an incompatibility for a custom quant path. We rolled back within 12 minutes; root cause is documented in the incident report, we'll attach.
[01:52] Emma: Ok, thanks. For our side we care about tail latency — p95 is 240ms for standard prompts but p99 jumps to 1.2s on heavier pipelines. We want to keep p99 under 900ms for critical flows.
[02:07] Sofia: Understood. For p99 reduction we recommend: smaller serving kernels for those pipelines, targeted batching, and using our prefix/KV caching more aggressively for repeated prompts. Marcus will propose config changes.
[02:21] Marcus: Quick note — there's room to shrink their quant profile on a few models without notable quality loss; we can test at 4-bit for some summarization use cases. That reduces token compute cost by ~22% in our benchmarks.
[02:35] Ravi: How risky is 4-bit quant for our legal/invoice prompts? Slight hallucination increases are a concern.
[02:41] Marcus: We'll A/B test — start with non-critical batches and run evals on your prompt set. If regression > 1.5% we'll rollback.
[02:52] Priya: On roadmap, upcoming features relevant to Cerulean: improved batching heuristics (May), expanded KV cache diagnostics in Console (mid-April), and Dedicated pilot program details (Q2). We'll share timelines.
[03:07] Emma: Dedicated pilot — can you recap? We have compliance reasons and want more predictable throughput.
[03:12] Sofia: Sure — Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with guaranteed throughput and data isolation. Pricing is a monthly commit; you can burst to hosted. For many customers it's a 3 month pilot then commit.
[03:25] Jenna: For us network egress and VPC peering are must-haves. What's included?
[03:30] Priya: Private networking (VPC peering), KMS integration support, audit logs — all available for Dedicated pilots. For on-prem we'd need a separate convo.
[03:41] Ravi: Timing — our security review for new infra takes 3-4 weeks. If we want Dedicated in Q2 it's tight.
[03:48] Sofia: Agreed, that's why a pilot now is recommended; it gives time for the security review while we validate cost/latency.
[03:58] Marcus: Back to optimizations — here's an action plan: 1) Marcus runs KV-cache benchmark with your sample traffic and looks at miss ratio; 2) we identify top prompts that would benefit from prefix caching; 3) test 4-bit quant on a copy of the model for non-critical workloads.
[04:18] Emma: We'll pull prompt set and a week's sample traffic, but we need to scrub PII first.
[04:24] Jenna: Also want a failover policy — if Dedicated falls below capacity we need graceful degradation to smaller models.
[04:30] Sofia: Yes, our smart routing can fallback to smaller model variants automatically — we'll demo that in the pilot.
[04:38] Ravi: Billing question — how do you handle overage for dedicated? We prefer predictable caps.
[04:43] Priya: Dedicated has commit tiers with bundled overage rules; we can map a commit that caps cost at a reasonable level and allow controlled bursts subject to approval. We'll include options in the pricing doc.
[04:55] Emma: One more thing — SSO mapping and RBAC for our users. We need admin-only access and separate API keys per team.
[05:03] Sofia: Supported — SAML SSO and per-team API keys with RBAC roles. We'll share our SSO integration guide.
[05:10] Marcus: Also note audit log retention can be extended for compliance packages. We'll include retention options and costs.
[05:18] Priya: Any other open items?
[05:21] Emma: Quality regression monitoring — we need alerts if summary drift increases beyond 2% on our evals. Is that configurable in Console?
[05:29] Priya: Yes, we can wire a regression alert to your eval sets and send Slack or email notifications. We'll set a baseline today and tune thresholds.
[05:37] Sofia: Ok let's go through the agreed next steps before we close.
[05:41] Sofia: Action items recap: Sofia to send cost breakdown and pricing options; Marcus to run KV-cache benchmarks and propose config changes; Priya to share roadmap and SLA docs; Emma to provide scrubbed prompt set and traffic sample.
[05:59] Ravi: Sounds good. If we get cost breakdown and pilot plan we can route to procurement and security.
[06:05] Sofia: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the notes and attachments.

(End of transcript)

References mentioned: incident report link (will be attached), Q2 roadmap doc (link), dedicated pilot one-pager (link), sample cost CSV (link).
